12274.title: Already somebody else’s concept? (sin traducir)
12274.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. (sin traducir) . The table’s labels are in the source language: it reports counts per scheme, computed by the gate rather than authored here. (sin traducir) . Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 3178 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 3178 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.

12275.title: Páginas
12275.content: Los candidatos extraídos no se traducen: se toman literalmente de los recursos del grafo de conocimiento y no están revisados. Sus páginas están en el idioma de origen. El glosario en el idioma de origen, con todos los términos extraídos.

12281.title: What a folio is
12281.content: The knowledge graph is four sub-graphs, and an instance declares which of them it holds. Content is what somebody authors and a reader reads — this layer’s subject. Skills are the instructions an agent follows to do the work. Processes are the BPMN diagrams that say who does what, in which order, and where the gates are — they are executable, not illustrations. Tools are what an agent can call. Getting anything in is acquisition: unstructured and semi-structured sources arrive through uploads/ or through the conversation, and are ingested into library/. It is a step rather than a graph kind of its own — there is no fifth directory to look for. Scope: the content model — what a folio IS. Not the skills and tools that operate on it, and not any particular folio’s chapters. | Content A document is structured prose; a paper adds the block kinds whose assertion is a formal claim. | Skills Every skill and role, and how they fit together. | Processes The BPMN diagrams, which are the source of truth rather than a picture of it. | Tools What an agent can call, served over MCP. | Acquisition How a source gets from uploads/ into library/. | RTFM — folio-assist-core Its scope, in and out, and why it declares no directories yet. | .

12287.title: Cuatro cosas, en orden
12287.content: 1. El plan de trabajo es donde dices lo que estás haciendo. No un mensaje de chat, no un comentario: beans, un almacén versionado que cualquier sesión o agente puede leer. Reclama antes de trabajar para que una sesión hermana no tome el mismo elemento; un bean que resulta no ser necesario se marca scrapped, con sus razones, y nunca se elimina. cat-harness/scripts/install-beans.sh && export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" beans list # lo que está abierto beans create "<title>" # …tras comprobar que el título no existe beans <id> --status in-progress # reclamarlo, de forma visible . 2. Crea tu primer folio. Este repositorio es la plataforma; tu contenido vive en el suyo propio. Un solo comando lo prepara — los manifiestos, la declaración, los archivos del agente y el enlace de vuelta aquí: . bun run init-folio --help . Después, Primeros pasos acompaña el primer bloque por la validación, el renderizado y la revisión. 3. Conoce qué tipo de cosa estás escribiendo. Un documento es prosa estructurada; un artículo (paper) es eso más los tipos de bloque cuya aserción es una afirmación formal, respaldada por Lean y compuesta con LaTeX. La elección decide qué bloques son válidos y qué controles se ejecutan: Tipos de contenido. 4. La documentación que nunca leerás. Toda ella — las guías de autoría, la arquitectura, el flujo de publicación, la referencia generada de esquemas y habilidades. Está aquí, es exhaustiva, y lo honesto es esperar que llegues a ella desde un buscador en el momento exacto en que algo se rompa. Es una buena forma de usarla. Los tres pasos de arriba son los que vale la pena leer ahora. Cuando lo que te desconcierta es la maquinaria y no la autoría — quién hace qué cosa, en qué proceso, con qué habilidad — empieza por La plataforma. Una sola frase allí sostiene todo el modelo, y cada palabra en ella es un objeto declarado por separado.

12288.title: ¿Qué es folio-assistant?
12288.content: folio-assistant es la plataforma — no contiene contenido. Proporciona las habilidades, los esquemas, las herramientas y un servidor MCP (Model Context Protocol) que un agente impulsado por LLM utiliza para planificar, redactar, validar, revisar, probar y publicar un folio de contenido que reside en un repositorio independiente. Separación de responsabilidades. Esta documentación describe el formalismo del marco de trabajo y cómo usar folio-assistant — mantenido deliberadamente separado de cualquier contenido específico. Cuando aparece contenido en estas páginas, es puramente ilustrativo (un ejemplo), nunca el artefacto canónico. flowchart LR A[Autor + LLM] -->|chat / herramientas MCP| B(folio-assistant) B --> C{Adaptador de contenido} C -->|artículo| D[Repositorio Lean + LaTeX] C -->|WHO SMART DAK| E[L2 BPMN / DMN / Excel] C -->|WHO SMART IG| F[L3 FHIR / FSH] B --> G[Habilidades + Esquemas + RBAC] D & E & F --> H[Sitio publicado / PDF / IG] .

12289.title: Tipos de contenido admitidos
12289.content: folio-assistant es extensible — cada tipo de contenido es gestionado por un adaptador de contenido y un paquete de habilidades correspondiente. Los tipos admitidos actualmente: . | Tipo de contenido | Artefactos | Paquete de habilidades | . | Artículos científicos y libros | Formalización Lean 4 + LaTeX/Markdown | authoring-math | . | Kits de adaptación digital (DAK) de las Directrices SMART de la OMS | Artefactos L2 — BPMN, DMN, diccionarios de datos Excel, personas | authoring-who-smart-guidelines | . | Guías de implementación SMART de la OMS | Recursos FHIR L3, FSH, salida de IG Publisher | authoring-who-smart-guidelines | . | Otros | Extensible — añade un nuevo adaptador + paquete de habilidades | Añadir un tipo de contenido | . El paquete transversal content-lifecycle (planificar → redactar → validar → revisar → probar → publicar → retroalimentación → retirar) se aplica a cada tipo de contenido. El flujo de publicación lo modela adecuadamente — como carriles BPMN, con los roles, la puerta de validación HCI y el plan de trabajo compartido.

12290.title: A dónde ir a continuación
12290.content: . | Instalación — requisitos previos, clonación, bun install, verificación de capacidades. | Primeros pasos — conecta el servidor MCP a tu LLM y ejecuta tu primera habilidad. | Tutorial: Redactar un artículo con folio-assistant — un recorrido completo guiado por LLM con una sesión de chat simulada. | Tipos de contenido — el formalismo de cada dominio de autoría. | Flujo de publicación — diagramas de carriles BPMN de los procesos de edición y publicación: la puerta de validación de HCI, quién revisa qué y el plan de trabajo compartido. | Incorporación del agente — orientación para un agente LLM situado en un folio: primeros pasos, búsqueda de habilidades, el modelo de objetos de contenido, sidecars de QA. | Habilidades y roles — cada habilidad y rol, y cómo interactúan junto con el LLM. | Referencia del esquema de habilidades — contratos de entrada/salida generados para cada habilidad. | Referencia de la API de TypeScript — el modelo de objetos de contenido (Block, Chapter, Paper, builders, restricciones Zod). | Arquitectura — adaptadores, servidor MCP, RBAC, el modelo de bloques. | El grafo de conocimiento — la taxonomía de subgrafos, en qué sentido van las referencias y cómo dividen el trabajo los repositorios. | The Harness — la instanciación, el recorrido de dependencias y a qué obliga incorporar un directorio al arnés. | . Vale la pena leer dos habilidades antes que las páginas anteriores, porque todo lo demás las asume: getting-started enruta lo que realmente estás intentando hacer, y placement determina a dónde pertenece un nuevo nodo antes de crearlo.

12294.title: Who declares each specification
12294.content: A user declares the specification it depends on; the record names no user. That is data-modelling step 8 — the dependent holds the pointer — and it is why this list cannot drift from the code: a file that stops declaring stops being listed. Four forms are read: a @conformsTo tag, a conformsTo: front-matter list, an xmlns binding, and a graph kind whose typing module declares the spec (bean u63y). Every declaration names a record on this page.

12297.title: External schemas
12297.content: A specification here is referenced, not held: the edition is named and the terms this repository actually acts on are materialised into the graph, but the document itself stays at the authority. That split is the owner’s: “dont need to materalize, but should reference specific version being used”, and “some schema that is operational should be in KG”. So each record answers three questions — which edition, what here depends on it, and which of its terms this repository branches on. 22specifications 106operative terms in the graph 224declared uses 0declarations naming no record

Where to drop a file — the queue's upload URL candidate, extracted Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the instance's own declaration: the uploads graph's directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub's /upload/<branch>/<path>. 12323.title: Glossary: Schema fields, M–R
12323.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms, the counts and the sources are on the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 28 (SKOS) · cat-harness 1774 (SKOS) · cat-openapi 13 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 75 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 127 (SKOS) · smart-base 9 (SKOS). One of 4 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 504 terms and is 284 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2026 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2026 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 504 shown . M N O P Q R

12331.title: Glossary: Schema fields, F–L
12331.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms, the counts and the sources are on the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 28 (SKOS) · cat-harness 1774 (SKOS) · cat-openapi 13 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 75 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 127 (SKOS) · smart-base 9 (SKOS). One of 4 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 386 terms and is 217 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2026 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2026 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 386 shown . F G H I J K L

12340.title: Glossary: Schema fields, A–E
12340.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms, the counts and the sources are on the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 28 (SKOS) · cat-harness 1774 (SKOS) · cat-openapi 13 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 75 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 127 (SKOS) · smart-base 9 (SKOS). One of 4 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 558 terms and is 316 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2026 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2026 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 558 shown . A B C D E

12347.title: Glossary: Schema fields, S–Z
12347.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms, the counts and the sources are on the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 28 (SKOS) · cat-harness 1774 (SKOS) · cat-openapi 13 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 75 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 127 (SKOS) · smart-base 9 (SKOS). One of 4 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 578 terms and is 320 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2026 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2026 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 578 shown . S T U V W

12354.title: Glossary: Schema fields
12354.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms, the counts and the sources are on the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 28 (SKOS) · cat-harness 1774 (SKOS) · cat-openapi 13 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 75 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 127 (SKOS) · smart-base 9 (SKOS). Split by first letter. 2026 terms are too many for one page within its budget of 1.0 MB, so they are on 4 pages by the first letter of the label. The ranges are fixed, so a term’s address does not move as terms are added. A label that does not start with a letter is on the first page. | A–E: 558 terms | F–L: 386 terms | M–R: 504 terms | S–Z: 578 terms | .

12356.title: Glossary: BPMN activities
12356.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms, the counts and the sources are on the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 440 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 31 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 116 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 10 (SKOS) · smart-base 19 (SKOS). Size: this page holds 661 terms and is 534 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 661 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 661 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. The content keeps only what its own checks need; the leak test's pending list is empty. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Hosted . 6 · Split content from tools candidate, extracted Create <name>-tools as a sibling directory and move the code: the Zod source, the generators, the README and diagram writers, the content checks. Cut its import cone to its own files and declared packages. Both start at the content's version. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Split . 6 · Validate [content-validate] candidate, extracted Schema and constraint checks over every block. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Task_Validate . 6 · Validate [content-validate] candidate, extracted Run content validation over the folio: schemas, the content profile (formal kinds only in a paper), cross-block consistency and that the Lean builds. Loop back rather than rendering over a failure. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/processes/content/authoring-a-paper.bpmn#Task_Validate . 7 · Plan publication candidate, extracted Every identifier the content mints is a file some step publishes: /<version>/ for what programs read, kept for every version; /v<major>/ for pages people read. Name collisions between published files are resolved here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Plan . 7 · Render MD / HTML / PDF [document-publishing] candidate, extracted Assemble to Markdown, then pandoc. The PDF goes through an HTML engine — never latexmk. Run latex_preflight first — missing packages, fonts or engine — rather than discovering them twenty minutes in. The preamble, class and macros belong to the folio, never to the platform. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/processes/content/authoring-a-paper.bpmn#Task_Render . 8 · Rehearse standalone candidate, extracted Copy the content and the tools alone into a temporary directory, with nothing else on the path, and run the tools' checks there. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Rehearse . 8 · Review and feedback [content-review] candidate, extracted The reviewer this folio binds. authoring-document relaxes the base SME step precisely because no single lane fits every document. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Task_Review . 8 · Review and feedback [content-review] candidate, extracted Review the rendered paper, not a description of it, and record the feedback. The outcome is iterate — back to authoring — or approved for the publication path. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/processes/content/authoring-a-paper.bpmn#Task_Review . 9 · Authorise the extraction candidate, extracted A repository cut changes the substrate every other process binds to; that is a person's decision. 12358.content: Abort, restore the tree, list what was refused candidate, extracted git merge --abort. Each refused path is listed with its pattern's reason, or "no declared pattern". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Abort . Accept it, and record where it came from candidate, extracted Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . Accept, or send back candidate, extracted The editor's lane, kept separate on purpose: the reviewer who judged the change is not the position that accepts it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Accessibility: measure, do not assert candidate, extracted Contrast COMPUTED against the real ground, including the worst case a backdrop can present; a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning (SC 1.4.1); an accessible name on every region; keyboard and focus order. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient — axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, and a CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Accessibility . Add an actor, and declare its kind candidate, extracted Human, agentic or mechanical. A userTask because the agentic/mechanical line is JUDGEMENT — role-model.md says so — and reading it wrong disqualifies the actor from every judgement task it exists to perform, silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AddActor . Address the review candidate, extracted Every finding is answered — implemented, or replied to with why not. A design question does not excuse skipping the nits in the same review. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_AddressReview . Adjudicate against the checker candidate, extracted The reviewer and a checker read the same claim differently — a disagreement about ONE kg-qa criterion (prose-claims-resolve). Descend into Process_CriterionAdjudication, which runs the shared adjudication and then one of its three outcomes: the checker's finding stands, the criterion is scoped, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The checker's entry is kept beneath the verdict rather than overwritten (requirement R4 of issue #1042). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/narrative-code-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate flagged passage (human reviewer) candidate, extracted A human SME or editor reviews the flagged passage. They may: - Accept the translation as-is (false positive) - Edit the translation and re-run QA - Reject and request re-translation The round trip establishes that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the conflict candidate, extracted A human or agentic decision, never a merge rule. Which side wins depends on why the local edit was made, and a process that picked automatically would be choosing without the one fact that decides it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the criterion disagreement candidate, extracted The shared judgement — entry condition, untainted dispatch, person-or-agent restriction — asked with THIS question's permitted answers. cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes sits here rather than on A_Adjudicate inside it because the answers depend on what was asked, and the gateway below is what acts on them: the engine refuses a mismatch between the two. Process_Adjudication may also leave at End_NotAdjudicable — one entry and no other side is a review or a gate, not a disagreement — in which case nothing below runs and there is nothing to record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted The judgement itself, and the one step nothing here can check: if a mechanism could decide it, the process would not have been entered. It declares NO cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on purpose, and that absence is the whole of bean bvuk. This step used to name three — stands, scope, dispensation — and six diagrams called it: review-narrative and voice-review, whose question those three answer, and four whose question they do not. refresh-materialized asks which side wins a local-vs-remote conflict; there is no criterion to scope there and no dispensation to grant, yet the outcome half ran regardless. Since the caller's question decides the permitted answers, the caller declares them: cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on its OWN call activity, with its own gateway acting on them. criterion-adjudication.bpmn is that for the QA-criterion question. What could NOT be fixed by passing the codes as data, which was this bean's first recommendation: the three branches ran three different TASKS, so a caller handed local-wins would have had it pointing at A_ScopeCriterion. The branches had to move, not the enum. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/adjudication.bpmn#A_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement [adjudication] candidate, extracted adjudication.bpmn. When the editor and a reviewer, or two reviewers, disagree about a finding, an adjudicator settles it and records why; the review comment moves to adjudicated with the Decision that closed it. Permitted answers (bean bvuk, owner 2026-09-23): stands — the finding is right and the author addresses it; withdrawn — the finding is wrong and the comment closes. Recorded on the comment, not branched: either way the flow goes on to the coverage check. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate the flagged passage candidate, extracted A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_FlagDrift . Adjudicate the voice findings candidate, extracted Three outcomes, all legitimate: the register is wrong for this genre; the criterion does not belong in this genre and should carry profiles; or the block is a stated exception and a reviewer entry records why. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_AdjudicateVoice . Adjudicate: prose, scope, or exception candidate, extracted The same three outcomes as the base voice axis. The register is wrong for this block (fix the prose); the rule does not apply to this content (scope it on the voice, one edit rather than ten overrules); or the rule applies and this block is an exception (a reviewer entry saying why). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudication candidate, extracted folio-assistant's adjudication: the adjudication leads, the checker's entry is kept, and the dispensation carries its reason. Reviewers disagreeing on ONE criterion is a criterion disagreement, so this calls the QA-criterion specialisation (bean bvuk, owner 2026-09-23): the failing entry stands, the criterion does not apply to this screen, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. FOR THIS CALLER THE SPLIT WAS A REGRESSION, not a fix, and that is worth keeping because the PR that made it said the opposite. When bvuk moved the outcome half out of adjudication.bpmn, #1074 reported that all four remaining callers "no longer reach A_ScopeCriterion or A_Dispensation" and framed it as the intended effect. True for three of them, whose question never admitted those steps. Here it removed the two steps the sentence above already documents, so the call was left pointing at a shared judgement that no longer runs either. Repointing restores what the documentation always claimed rather than changing it. The entry condition matches exactly rather than approximately: GW_Agree asks whether the blind reviewers' entries agree and takes no here, and Process_CriterionAdjudication starts at "entries for one criterion disagree" — R_Review records pass, warn or fail PER CRITERION with a reason, so the disagreement reaching this step is a per-criterion disagreement between reviewer entries and nothing else. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Admit it to the train, record the train id candidate, extracted Writes the queue entry's trainId and placement (rule, class, rank) with who decided and when. A decision, so it is stored; the facts it was decided on are not. PRECONDITION, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the worktree carries no untracked, non-ignored file before the member is merged and the tree regenerated. git status --porcelain must be empty. The reason is specific: generated directory READMEs carry a per-subdirectory file count, and the writer counts the files GIT WOULD COMMIT -- git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard (bootstrap-tools/scripts/git-files.ts:23). --exclude-standard already keeps IGNORED junk out, which is the __pycache__ case that drove that line, but --others still counts an untracked file nobody has ignored. So a transient written by an earlier train step moves a committed count, readme:subgraphs:check goes red, and the red belongs to nobody. Train 6 hit this. The count is volatile for a second reason the precondition cannot fix: two members each adding a file write different integers to one line. Measured in bean y7b3 -- 76 of 300 replayed merges conflicted on beans/README.md, every one on the | defs/ | N files | line -- and the exposure is wider than that bean states: 54 generated READMEs across 14 instances carry 207 such rows (measured 2026-10-02). merge:main already resolves them (readme-generated-regions), so the cost falls on merges made by plain git. The chosen fix is bean ba9e: take the integer off main into the KG's _data layer, which classifies take-base and is therefore auto-resolved, leaving the README with a marker that is invariant until the directory crosses LIST_LIMIT. Not done here -- it spans the pinned bootstrap-tools submodule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Admit . Adopt the version bump candidate, extracted The reusable subprocess. Every pinned dependency enters it the same way, so a new tenant is a registry row and a call — never a second diagram saying the same thing in different words. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Call_Adopt . Adopt, hold or decline candidate, extracted A PERSON decides. The lane admits person only, so activity-fulfilment-kind fails the moment somebody makes an agent the accepting party, and relaxable="false" means no package may relax the step. The publication manager rather than the editor because a pin is not a change to the corpus — it is a change to what the published artefact is BUILT FROM, and that role is the one accountable for what is live. Deliberately NOT a DMN-backed gateway. Every computed gateway in this repository reduces to arithmetic over tool output; this one weighs a rendering nobody can score against the cost of staying behind, and a table here would look authoritative without being so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#PM_Decide . Agent review of the change [content-review] candidate, extracted A review agent judges what no checker can: accuracy, voice, exposition, whether the change says what the editor meant. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_AgentReview . Alert the publication manager [publish-verification] candidate, extracted Process_PublishAlert — the ONE alert every failing step after the publish button goes through, whichever step it was. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Call_Alert . Announce the branch on the issue candidate, extracted On CREATING the feature branch, comment on the issue: the branch name, the process and phase, and the beans claimed. Visibility is the whole point — without it a sibling session or a human cannot tell that work has begun, only that it has finished. Deliberately on this edge and not inside Phase 6. The three loops back into A_Implement (increment rejected, MVP not ready, feedback translated) re-enter implementation on the SAME branch, and re-announcing on each would be noise. Announce once, when the branch is created. Before announcing, run the collision review that starts any new unit of work (coordinate, "Starting new work"): open PRs and in-progress beans checked against the branch's files and subject, scaled to the blast radius, and the result recorded in the bean before the first edit. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_AnnounceBranch . Answer, decline, or say nothing candidate, extracted The Requestor's move. Declining is an answer. Saying nothing is not, and is what the recommendation's "if there is no answer" was for. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_Answer . Append removed with the reason candidate, extracted BEFORE the removal, not after: a job that dies mid-step must leave a record of the intent rather than an artefact that vanished with no entry. A reason is REQUIRED — an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity this log exists to prevent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRemoved . Append rendered candidate, extracted A re-deploy is a rendering, so it gets its own entry rather than overwriting the last. "When was this last built" is then answerable without diffing commits. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRendered . Append rendered to the render log candidate, extracted Its OWN commit, not part of the deploy. The publish action writes only into destination_dir, so an entry riding in _site would land at STAGING/<slug>/_render-log/ — inside the directory a cleanup removes, which is the one place a record of the removal must not be. continue-on-error: a preview that deployed and whose entry did not is a gap in the record, not a failed deploy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_LogRendered . Append restored candidate, extracted A full-replace deploy (docs-site.yml, the only publisher without keep_files) wipes the branch; restore-staging carries the previews AND this log back in. Its own event rather than a second rendered, because "somebody pushed this branch" and "an unrelated merge nearly deleted it" are different facts — and bean plj1 is what happens when the second is invisible. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRestored . Append retained with the reason candidate, extracted THE ENTRY THAT MAKES THE LOG WORTH READING. A preview still standing because a signal fired leaves no trace otherwise, and the next person asking "why is this still up" has nothing to consult. A reason is REQUIRED — the tool refuses without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRetained . Append retained, with why it stays candidate, extracted The event that makes the log worth reading. A removal was CONSIDERED and refused; without an entry that leaves no trace on the branch at all, and the next person asking *"why is this preview still up"* has only a comment on a pull request that may itself be closed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_LogRetained . Append WHO disclaimer (if DAK) candidate, extracted For WHO SMART Guidelines content, automatically appends the WHO legal disclaimer: - Translation not created by WHO - English edition is authoritative original - WHO not responsible for translation accuracy Only applies when folio contentType includes WHO/DAK content. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_AppendDisclaimer . Apply it, and state each option's trade-offs candidate, extracted Follow the selected methodology as written — adopted whole, not blended with another. At least two real options: one option is not a choice, and a straw option is worse than a short list because it makes the analysis look thorough while narrowing it. Never quantify the comparison to make it look measured. Where a method scores and sums, this platform takes the structure and refuses the arithmetic: the weights are invented and a total reads as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/options-analysis.bpmn#A_Apply . Apply the stated default, and say so candidate, extracted Only the default stated in A_Recommend, only where the caller allows one, and recorded as assumed with the default named — never as the person's answer. The next message to the person says it was applied, so they can reverse it. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_ApplyDefault . Appraise and grade the body of evidence candidate, extracted Certainty of evidence per the grading system the folio declares. The grade attaches to the BODY of evidence for one PICO question, not to an individual citation -- which is why this step is after the join and not inside the fan-out. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_AppraiseGrade . Approve candidate, extracted The committee approves the change: the judgement, recorded with the evidence it rests on. Approving is not merging. They were one task ("Approve and merge") until bean en2d split them, because a self-authored change cannot be approved through GitHub's own review (the approver may not be the PR's author), and a merge needs the owner's explicit confirmation whoever approved. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_Approve . Approve requirements candidate, extracted Stakeholders approve the requirements and impact analysis on the issue, or send them back for revision. Only their approval moves the work to sign-off; an agent never records an approval on a person's behalf. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#S_ApproveReqs . ARCHIVAL verify fixity — never re-fetch candidate, extracted Re-compute the digest and compare. An archive is NEVER re-fetched — the source is what it exists to survive, so replacing it with today's version discards the state it was keeping. A mismatch means OUR copy rotted, and the remedy is restoration from a backup, not re-download. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Fixity . Archive → greppable contents manifest candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED. Tracked as a bean; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Tar/zip is opaque to every grep in the corpus until its contents are listed as data. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Archive . Ask BA to create or link issue candidate, extracted Ask — never create. Creating an issue without the BA's permission is the thing this step exists to prevent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_AskCreate . Ask first about what could not be determined candidate, extracted The caller's question waits, and is counted ("one more question after this"). What is put first is the undetermined one: the context you could not establish, the Role you are not sure you hold, or the Process you cannot place this in. It goes through the same order as any question — say what you determined and what you could not, the candidates you see, the one you would pick and why — and it allows NO default: a Process or Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave. With more than one undetermined, ask about the outermost first (the Process before the Role before the context), since the outer answer usually settles the inner. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_AskUndeterminedFirst . Ask ONE question candidate, extracted One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. Uses whatever channel the caller is in — in bootstrap, the conversation the person is already in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_PutQuestion . Ask the owner on the PR, both sides quoted candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_AskOwner . Ask the person to do what only they can candidate, extracted A step the agent cannot do or cannot check from here — switching Pages on without a signed-in gh, granting a permission, choosing between two ways of fixing a declaration. Asked through the one reusable discussion, with the exact step written out so it can be followed without opening anything else. A person saying "done" is recorded as their word, not as a check; the next run checks it. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_AskPerson . Ask the Requestor: which harness, and where? candidate, extracted The candidates go in as the options; the recommendation may name one; the default is NONE. What A_DetermineWhere established goes in too — the process, the two roles, the context — so the called discussion checks it rather than re-deriving it; and anything it could not establish goes in as undetermined, to be asked first. The Requestor's answer comes back as answered, or the question as still open. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_AskRequestor . Ask who is acting candidate, extracted The one step that needs a person. Asked ONCE and recorded, never re-asked: interaction/interaction.json and the record exist so that a preference stated once is not requested again, which is WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_AskWhoIsActing . Ask, per open PR, whether its HEAD has a run — skipping heads younger than 15 min candidate, extracted Run check:prs-have-runs --min-age-minutes 15, writing the report file first. A head younger than 15 minutes legitimately has no run yet and is skipped. Exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 could not determine; an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is treated as could-not-determine. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/pr-checks-present.bpmn#Task_Sweep . Assemble and validate the DAK [content-validate] candidate, extracted Assemble the validated components and run content validation: schemas, cross-component consistency and terminology bindings. The smart-base extractors read the authored artefacts; with SMART_BASE_HOME unset they report skip, never a clean run. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_AssembleDak . Assemble the site (template · Jekyll) [ig-publication] candidate, extracted Assemble the site from the merged records: the IG template and a Jekyll build over output/. Only site assembly happens here — every artefact record already exists. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Site . Assess downstream impact candidate, extracted Agent reviews downstream implications: - Will indicators need adjustment? - Will referral/follow-up for next visit be impacted? - Are translations affected (re-extract POT)? - Do Lean proofs still hold? skill: integration-watcher, translation-manager . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_AssessImpact . Assign to qualified human translator candidate, extracted The coordinator assigns the translation to a qualified translator, ideally a domain SME for the content area. For WHO content, the translator should be familiar with WHO SMART Guidelines terminology. The assignment includes: - The .pot file(s) from extraction - The domain glossary - Context notes (block kind, chapter, content area) - The deadline . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_AssignTranslator . Attach the evidence to the recommendation [content-author] candidate, extracted The PICO, the graded body of evidence, each verified citation and its resolved authority record are written onto the recommendation block, so a reader can retrace the whole chain from the sentence back to the source. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_AttachEvidence . Attest the pair, with a reason candidate, extracted The prose holds: record it with bun run pairs:attest -- --sidecar … --by agent|human --reason "…", naming what was compared. The attestation moves the pair's baseline to the current hashes, so the staleness flag clears and stays cleared until the code moves again. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/narrative-code-review.bpmn#A_Attest . Attribute the failure: each member's own CI first candidate, extracted T2 (SQ19 §2.1 pp. 2-3). A member whose own PR CI is red, or never ran on its head, is the prime suspect, and the evidence is already on GitHub. Only when every member is green alone is the failure a real conflict between them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Attribute . Audit the code nodes the increment adds candidate, extracted Descend into the review task for what this increment CHANGED IN THE GRAPH — Tool definitions in tools/ and schema definition nodes under schemas/. Build the entry [tree + manifest] candidate, extracted First the working copy is produced (qa:refresh, bean 3hk4): while the checkout still tracks test/results/, the commit's own copy is the record and nothing runs; once it does not, every declared QA writer runs into the empty tree, because the gates are in judge mode and wrote nothing a publish could carry. Exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs (names which input), 2 cannot-tell. Run against the BASE revision's checkout. Check the JSON Schemas and JSON-LD are at their IRIs candidate, extracted THE PRIMARY STEP of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness (owner, 2026-09-30: "json(ld) is primary step in initializing KG harness"), and so the first one checked once the declarations are read. Every JSON Schema the harness publishes (its $id) and every JSON-LD document (its vocabulary, its diagram vocabulary, its graph export, each carrying its own @context) is at the address it names under iriBase, where a program following the IRI finds it. Two checks: that the site build stages each one at its address, and that each address answers. A 404 is not published; a 403 or no answer from here could not be determined. The Pages site is the vehicle: when the documents are not yet answering, the site steps below are how they get there, and the report leads with this step's state. Check the selected methodology's evidence base candidate, extracted Before applying a methodology, establish that the thing being applied is what it claims to be. A methodology is adopted because it is somebody else's named, external work; this step checks that the origin it cites resolves to a source in a declared library, and reads the methodology-evidence QA sidecar for it. WHY THE CHECK IS HERE AND NOT AT ADOPTION. Adoption happens once; selection happens every time a decision is made. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. It does two things: it runs literature-search to try to close the gap, and it puts the evidence state into the record A_Record writes, so a reader can tell a decision made on a verified method from one made on a citation nobody could follow. The third state is the one that matters. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last.
