The issue closes only on their authorisation — an agent never closes an issue on its own say-so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#BA_Confirm . Confirm needs statement candidate, extracted Stakeholders confirm, on the issue, that the needs statement says what they need — or say what to change. A stakeholder's judgement; an agent does not record it for them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#S_ConfirmNeeds . Confirm the cardinalities candidate, extracted An operational question, asked of the people who run the process because they know where the exceptions are. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#S_ConfirmCardinality . Confirm the entities are the ones meant candidate, extracted A naming question. The BA owns the domain vocabulary; the agent does not guess, which is CRDM's own rule for phase 1 and applies here with more force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#BA_ConfirmEntities . Consolidate findings candidate, extracted One report from however many subprocesses ran. Findings are advice: a reviewer cannot accept the change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_Consolidate . Consolidate into 2-4 themes, with a recommendation each candidate, extracted Group by what the work delivers, not by agent. Each theme gets its epic, members, dependencies, risk, and one of: continue, fold in, new epic, park, scrap (owner only). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#A_Consolidate . Coordinate? How? candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/related-work.bpmn#U_Coordinate . COPYRIGHT per bitstream, and for the derived work candidate, extracted What the licence permits for THIS bitstream, and separately whether it permits the derivation. LICENSE-CONTENT.md exists in this repository and the ingestion pipeline does not read it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Copyright . Create feature branch candidate, extracted Agent creates a feature branch from main. Branch naming: feature/<short-description> Opens a PR immediately (AGENTS.md: "open the PR at the first commit"). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_CreateBranch . Create the bean (agent CLI, not an engine op) candidate, extracted beans create "<title>". This is the AGENT's call. The workflow engine has no create op — its vocabulary is claim, note and resolve, all of which act on an instance's existing bean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Create . Create the repositories candidate, extracted The owner creates the content and tools repositories and their Pages. Nothing is committed to them before this. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Create . Create the repository candidate, extracted Only on the new-repo branch, and only after the user has named it. An empty working directory is scaffolded in place instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_CreateRepo . Cross the axes into SO, WO, ST, WT candidate, extracted The TOWS matching step, and the only step that produces anything actionable. Strengths and weaknesses across, opportunities and threats down, and each cell names the strategy the pairing implies: SO — achieve opportunities that greatly match the strengths; WO — overcome weaknesses to attain opportunities; ST — use strengths to reduce vulnerability to threats; WT — prevent weaknesses, to avoid becoming more susceptible to threats. A SWOT that stops at four lists is the failure the source names as its central one. This step is what the process exists to reach. It produces CANDIDATE strategies, not a chosen one, and they are not ranked — see the process documentation on why no scoring activity exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_Cross . Cut the subgraph that leaves candidate, extracted Apply the editorial scope mechanically and report what it removed. A selection that reports nothing cannot be told from one that ran over an empty rule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Select .

12361.title: D
12361.content: Data dictionary and core data elements [l2-dak-authoring] candidate, extracted Author the data dictionary and core data elements for this component. Stay structured but not FHIR: a data element a clinician can review, from which L3 can later be derived rather than written twice. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_DataDict . Data model Entities + cardinalities candidate, extracted Between requirements and sign-off, and the order is the argument: requirements are statements about things, and the model says what the things ARE. Drafted earlier it is invented from nothing, since the entities come from the phase-2 BPA; drafted later, sign-off approves requirements whose nouns were never pinned — which is how two stakeholders approve one sentence meaning different things. Owner, 2026-09-20. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_DataModel . Decide each theme candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#U_Decide . Decide what may leave the repository candidate, extracted EDITORIAL, and it is stage 1 rather than a filter bolted to the exporter. kg-export produces the WHOLE graph because inspection wants the whole graph; a portal wants what its readers may see. Running the second as the first is how a QA verdict, a bean's blocking note or an unpublished draft reaches a public cache. Decided once, here, rather than at each consumer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#E_Scope . Decision logic · DMN tables [dmn-authoring] candidate, extracted Author the decision logic as DMN tables, within the FEEL subset the interpreter implements (any, literals, comparisons, one-of). Ranges, not() and function calls are refused at load, so write inside the subset. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_Dmn . Declare the model where a tool can read it candidate, extracted A model in prose is a proposal; a model in the declaration is a model. Ship a reader in the same change — everything here that was only documentation went inert within weeks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare the node materialized candidate, extracted The node's state moves from referenced to materialized, carrying purpose, localPath, gates and (archival) fixity. There is NO default state: a node that has not said is invalid, because 'the author did not say' and 'the author said they could not tell' are different facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the purpose: working or archival candidate, extracted working or archival, and it is asked FIRST because three of the five gates mean different things under each. An archival copy keeps the original bytes, never expires, requires fixity, and is the only thing that discharges sourceLoss; a working copy keeps derived content and discharges none of that. A process that gated first and asked afterwards would be judging a copy whose obligations it did not yet know. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Purpose . Deduplicate, and keep what is actually relevant candidate, extracted The paper's Refiner. Accumulates into the evidence set the report is built from — so what is dropped here is invisible downstream, which is why it is a step somebody performs rather than a filter buried in retrieval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Refine . Deploy the MVP to staging candidate, extracted An MVP is shared AS A STAGING DEPLOY, not as a description of one. feature-staging.yml publishes the branch under STAGING/<branch-slug>/ on gh-pages and comments the URL on the PR, so the stakeholder who tests it is looking at the built artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work. Measured in this repo on 2026-09-16: holding a rendered change back for assessment made assessment harder, not safer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_DeployStaging . Deploy the preview site [content-publish] candidate, extracted A preview never seeds the shared cache. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_DeployPreview . Deploy the rendering candidate, extracted Commit the staged tree onto gh-pages as a full replace (the instance's Pages workflow on a push to main, or by hand); GitHub Pages then builds it from the branch. Rebuild and retry on a rejected push; never rebase the branch. The gh-pages commit SHA is the message the report names. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Deploy . Deploy the site [content-publish] [ig-publication] candidate, extracted Deploy the site built from main or a release. Deploying is release-management, after a human authorised the release — an agent never records that authorisation. Report the published URL only once it answers: a returned deploy is not a serving site. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Deploy . Deploy to STAGING/<slug>/ candidate, extracted peaceiris/actions-gh-pages deploys to gh-pages branch under STAGING/<branch-slug>/ with keep_files: true so other staging deployments and the main site are preserved. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DeployStaging . Derive content from the assets [document-intake] candidate, extracted See ingest-derive-content.bpmn. Most of this subprocess is not implemented yet. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Derive . Derive the key [main/<sha> or pr/<n>/<sha>] candidate, extracted qa:publish --github reads the event: a push to main publishes under main/<sha>/, a pull request under pr/<n>/<head-sha>/ — the head that was tested, not the merge ref. It also reads whether the token can write, which the gateway after it routes on. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/qa-publish.bpmn#Task_DeriveKey . Derive the slug from the head ref candidate, extracted Derive the slug from the PR's head ref: every character outside [a-zA-Z0-9._-] becomes '-', runs of '-' collapse, and leading or trailing '-' is trimmed. It must be one safe path segment, checked by value. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Slug . Describe the desired change candidate, extracted Author describes the content change in natural language. Example: "Update the immunization schedule to add a booster at 18 months." . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the intended change candidate, extracted The editor states the change in natural language; no content has moved yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the need (chat, issue, discussion) candidate, extracted The BA describes the capability gap in their own words. They do not need to know it is called CRDM. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#BA_Submit . Detect change scope & impact candidate, extracted Agent analyses the requested change: - Which content blocks are affected? - Are there downstream implications (indicators, referral logic, visit schedules)? - Will deterministic logic (CQL/DMN) need updating? skill: content-graph, integration-watcher . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DetectScope . Detect feature request (crdm-detect skill) candidate, extracted Recognise the request as a platform capability change rather than content work, from crdm-detect's signals. Never call it "CRDM" to the person. Mid-content-work, ask whether to pause for requirements now or record a bean for later — do not switch on your own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#A_Detect . Detect media type and mint a doc id [document-intake] candidate, extracted Sniff the media type rather than trusting the extension, and mint the doc id from the page-1 arXiv stamp where there is one, else from the filename. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Detect . Detect the interaction modality candidate, extracted Before the first question is asked, establish HOW to ask it: audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for a user with limited hand function, large-type for low vision. A user who finds the questions unusable never reaches the rest of this diagram. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_DetectModality . Determine appropriate digital health interventions candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 4. Select interventions for the prioritized challenges, assess whether the enabling environment can support them, identify functional requirements and user stories, map the future-state workflow, and check whether existing applications already meet the requirements. The interventions CONSIDERED AND NOT CHOSEN are part of the output, with why — methodology-adoption's fourth refusal. A deleted alternative leaves the next reader unable to tell a decision from an oversight. Selection is from the Classification, and the who-digital-health voice governs the naming: an intervention is a capability, not the software that delivers it. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_DetermineInterventions . Determine the context: what is known, and already decided candidate, extracted Before composing anything: what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs the matter (the instance's <name>.json, the diagram the caller is in, the Skill its task names); what state is recorded; and whether the question has ALREADY been decided — by the person earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes their ruling. A settled question is not asked again: asking it reopens a decision and spends the person's attention twice. Read it, do not remember it: cite what you read. What the caller handed in is checked here, not re-derived. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineContext . Determine the process and task, or that you are idle candidate, extracted Name the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to, and say so in the message: "Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent". A reader who does not know which process you are in will assume the last one's rules still hold. If you are in no Process, that is an answer too: you are IDLE, and what you are doing is classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to — say that, rather than presenting a question as though a step had asked for it. You are OUT of process, and it is undetermined, when you cannot name the instance, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand was not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineProcess . Determine the roles: which you act as, and the person's candidate, extracted An Actor performs a task in a Process AS a Role. Nothing is a Role by nature: the same agent is the Bootstrapping Agent in one diagram and another Role in the next, and which one it is depends on the lane of the task it is performing now. So say which Role you are acting as — the lane of the CALLING task, since this lane is variable — and which Role the person you ask holds (the Requestor, or whoever the calling lane names). It decides what you may ask them for: only the Requestor chooses a harness, and a question put to somebody who does not hold the decision gets an answer that settles nothing. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineRoles . Determine where you are: process, roles, context candidate, extracted Before narrowing, say where this is happening, in the words you will use in the question. PROCESS: Initialize a harness, at its first step, inside Determine the harness and repositories — the only place a Bootstrapping Agent can be (FR-2). If you cannot say that (you were started some other way, or a step you believed done is not), you are out of process: do not infer your way back in. ROLES: you act as the Bootstrapping Agent because you were told so; the person you will ask is the Requestor — the one who asked for the harness, and the only one who may choose it. A request relayed by somebody else leaves the Requestor undetermined. CONTEXT: what the request said, and what the checkout holds — a declaration at its root, a harness named in the request. Whatever cannot be determined is handed to the called discussion as undetermined, and asked about first; it is never filled with a default. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineWhere . Determine which harness, and where candidate, extracted The candidates are listed and the Requestor is asked, in discussion, which asks through human-agent-discussion. IN: nothing but the context this agent was handed. OUT: zero or ONE harness, and the locations — a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json. One at most: a list of two is not an answer, and the Bootstrapping Agent may not break the tie itself. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_DetermineHarness . Develop a budget candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 7. Phases of implementation, cost drivers, and the budget matrix. This is the chapter that turns the preceding six into a COSTED implementation plan, which is the artefact the whole Guide exists to produce and the one a funder reads. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_DevelopBudget . Diff base → head and render the delta pages [ig-ast-delta] candidate, extracted ig-ast.ts diff <base> <head> --plan plan.json --site <site>/ast-delta/: resources added, removed, changed (with an element-level differential) and version-changed; edges added and removed; the plan's decision. Every page opens with the provisional mark and is wrapped in raw so narrative Liquid is not executed. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn#Task_Diff . Discard all entries, or a whole session candidate, extracted Remove every entry, one session's, or those before a date — emptyLog with { all }, { session } or { before }; there is no default selector. A file that will not parse is kept, and the result must say what was refused and why, not only what was removed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_EmptyAll . Discard one entry by id candidate, extracted Remove one entry by its stable id, with emptyLog({ id }). Logs are the one exception to the never-delete rule because an entry records no decision; the exception covers files that declare folio-log/v1, not the directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_EmptyOne . Dispatch one agent, recorded on the bean candidate, extracted Before the agent starts: the date, why the fail condition fired, the agent's id, its budget. Never while the first writer may still be live. Two failed attempts with the same cause go to the owner instead. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Dispatch . Dispatch with adjudicator_sees — never the artefact candidate, extracted UntaintedDispatch on the criterion declares what each party is given; the caller names a subject and a criterion and does not hand-assemble a brief, because the party composing a brief by hand is the producer. untaintedPartitionDefects reports overlap when the checker and the adjudicator can read the same file — one of them is then grading its own input, and the verdict measures nothing while raising no error. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/adjudication.bpmn#A_Dispatch . Do it, then check again candidate, extracted Only what the agent, or a tool it has, can do without replacing anything somebody wrote: regenerate a README section, add a missing Pages workflow, switch Pages on with an authenticated gh. Performing is not the same as done: the flow goes back to the check, and only the check says done. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_PerformStep . Do the work candidate, extracted The task itself. This diagram says nothing about how it is done; it only brackets it, so that a reader of the log can tell where one run of work began and ended. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_DoWork . Draft the block edit [content-author] candidate, extracted The authoring agent produces a PROPOSED change. Nothing is written to the corpus yet. For a rendered change it also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) here, before Gateway_ValidationFork, so the preview exists when the parallel review starts. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DraftEdit . Draft, review and publish [content-publish] candidate, extracted See draft-to-publication.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#CallActivity_Publication . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Drain . Drop its positions and sweep orphans candidate, extracted Only after the content has moved: drop its positions from the layout layer and sweep any position whose note is now gone. Sweeping first would make the board authoritative over the folio for one step. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_UpdateLayer . Drop the file in the queue candidate, extracted Through the forge's upload form, a commit, or any other route that lands the file in the declared queue. The agent watches rather than chases: an arrival may be minutes or days away. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#P_Upload .

12362.title: E
12362.content: Edit deterministic logic (if needed) candidate, extracted If the content change affects decision logic, indicators, or workflows: - Update CQL expressions - Update DMN decision tables - Adjust indicator definitions skill: dak-authoring, fhir-pipeline . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_EditLogic . Edit it in place — it is your own content candidate, extracted The ordinary path, drawn so the process does not read as though every edit needs a copy. Content in a writable directory is authored content and is edited where it lives; the copy-out is for somebody else's bytes, not for yours. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_EditDirectly . Edit narrative content blocks candidate, extracted Agent modifies the relevant content blocks (.md files, block manifests). Validates each edit against the schema (content_validate). skill: content editing, block builders . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_EditContent . Edit the flagged passage and re-inject candidate, extracted The reviewer corrects the passage in the PO rather than sending the whole translation back. Flows to Task_PoInject, so the round-trip QA runs again over the corrected text — "edit the translation and re-run QA", which is what the adjudication step has always offered and what this process could not do. A userTask, not a service task: this is the one step here where a person edits content, and the lane's actor is the reviewer who just adjudicated. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_EditTranslation . Editing and HCI validation [content-author] candidate, extracted See editing-hci-validation.bpmn. Runs once per proposed change, not once per cycle. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#CallActivity_Editing . Editing and HCI validation [content-author] candidate, extracted The editing sub-process. Every change to the corpus goes through its HCI validation gate — a red draft is fixed there, never by patching the built artifact. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#CallActivity_Editing . Eject the culprit, record why candidate, extracted T1 (R3; SQ19 §2.2 p. 3): the culprit leaves, the rest re-run. Writes ejection on its queue entry (train id, reason, evidence URL, when) and a dated evidence snapshot on this instance. The train is never rejected whole for one member. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Eject . End-to-end + accessibility (HARD) candidate, extracted Install Chromium, check the rendered BPMN SVGs are current, then run the Playwright suite, which includes the accessibility checks. Hard: a failure blocks the PR. SHARDED since bean dlqu (drawn as one task, deliberately: a multi-instance marker would add a BPMN term to every instance's UML overview, about 75 generated files, for a picture this sentence already gives): the suite runs as three e2e-shard jobs (E2E_SHARD=i/3, one Playwright worker per core in each), and the e2e job that carries this check's name completes the task only when every instance succeeded — a shard that failed, was cancelled or never ran is a red check, never a skipped one. Measured before the split: playwright test alone was 4m33s of a 5m16s job, the workflow's slowest once bun test ran in parallel. The BPMN-render and .bat-wrapper checks run in shard 1 only, so they are asked once. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-quality-gates.bpmn#Task_E2E . Ensure the publication-manager label candidate, extracted The alert is a tracking issue labelled publication-manager — the role, not a person, because no actor declares a GitHub account for it. Whoever watches that label is alerted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/publish-alert.bpmn#A_Label . Ensure the tracking label exists candidate, extracted Create the ci-health label with --force so it exists before either issue path runs — the close path filters on it too, and on a repository that has never had a finding it would not exist yet. Skipped on an unknown verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/ci-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Label . Ensure the tracking label exists candidate, extracted Create the pr-no-checks label with --force so it exists before either issue path runs — the close path filters on it too, and on a repository that has never had a finding it would not exist yet. Skipped on an unknown verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/pr-checks-present.bpmn#Task_Label . Ensure the tracking label exists candidate, extracted Create the repo-health label with --force so it exists before either issue path runs — the close path filters on it too, and on a repository that has never had a finding it would not exist yet. Skipped on an unknown verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/repository-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Label . ENUMERATE + SUBSET against the source descriptor candidate, extracted Resolve the request against the source's descriptor (one per corpus, in the declared sources/ of the instance that owns it, e.g. who-iris/sources/), read against cat-harness/schemas/source-descriptor.ts BEFORE any gate. Three things come from it and none may be guessed. (1) Which subset strategies the source supports — supportsSubset(). (2) Whether a subset stands on its own: when subsetIsSelfContained is false (mathlib), the request is closed over its dependencies here, and every gate after this one is asked about the CLOSURE, because a subset that omits what its members depend on is not a smaller corpus, it is one that does not build. (3) What enumerating the whole costs — enumerationCost(), which is undefined when the descriptor has no measured denominator; SIZE then refuses rather than estimates. A source with no descriptor is not an error here: it is an unknown, and SIZE refuses on it. Bean w5bn: the descriptor is CALLED here rather than restated. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Enumerate . Establish origin and licence candidate, extracted Authors, publication, identifier, and the licence the source itself states. No stated licence means reference only: headings, page ranges and a summary in our own words; the file stays in uploads/ (git-ignored) pinned by checksum. A method with no origin is a house process; write a skill instead. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/methodology-from-source.bpmn#A_Origin . 12364.title: G
12364.content: Gather and verify the evidence [evidence-retrieval] candidate, extracted Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate's authority resolved against its publisher's own API. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none -- and is skipped there rather than satisfied vacuously. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#CallActivity_Evidence . Give a link, a description, or neither candidate, extracted "Or neither" is a real outcome, not a failure. The ask says what happens if nothing comes, and then that happens — the work proceeds without the resource and says so. Grant a dispensation, with its reason candidate, extracted The rule applies and this subject is a stated exception. A kind: "human" entry with result: "pass" overrides the script's fail for that criterion, and ONLY while its field_hash matches the current source — so the dispensation is scoped to the version it was granted against, lapses when the block changes, and never becomes precedent. There is nothing to overturn later; the source moving overturns it. A dispensation with no notes is not a dispensation. It is an override somebody applied to get to green, and nobody can review it afterwards — which is why this step is not relaxable. For the theme: docs/assets/js/docs-ui.js MOVES the theme's own search markup into the action launcher and binds .search, #search-input and .search-label; docs-ui.css overrides .side-bar, .site-header and .main-header; three e2e specs assert the structure the theme emits. An upstream rename of any of those is not a build failure — it is a shipped feature that quietly stops working. Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. 12367.title: J
12367.content: Judge the assets in their design candidate, extracted A person looks at the ingested assets laid out in the design they are for, at BOTH a web and a mobile width. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, and that is stated rather than hidden: ingest-theme.bpmn used to refuse to call this process for exactly that reason. The owner's ruling puts theme review at ingestion only, and a ruling that moves a review does not remove the person who performs it — so ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else stays unattended because Gateway_ThemeSource routes it past. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. Three defects in the landing board — a selector matching nothing, a crop cutting the subject, a fade wrong in both directions — were invisible to a clean build, a passing suite and every gate, and were found only by rendering the page and looking. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#R_Judge .

12368.title: K
12368.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the local edit, and re-pin so it stops being asked candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

12369.title: L
12369.content: L1 completeness gate candidate, extracted See ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn. Skill-backed by library-ingestion (2026-09-30, bean 7bg9): its section "What a complete L1 entry holds" names check:l1-complete as the gate and states its three results. Until then this step named paper-relevance-triage, which never existed, and was left uncovered rather than bound to a guess. The gate contains one adjudication (Task_FlagDrift: real, spurious or source-wrong), and its own Task_Verdict records the answer as a reason against the verdict before returning. So both answers reach this step, and nothing here branches on them; Gateway_Complete branches on the gate's completeness verdict instead. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Gate . Land it in library/ candidate, extracted A permanent sample joins the library as an L1 source, with the materialization record (purpose, gates, fixity) beside it. From here refresh-materialized governs it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Library . Land the bytes in the copier's own folio/ candidate, extracted Into the copier's own declared folio/, never a scratch area — a directory nobody declared is a directory nobody gates, and the copy would be publishable by accident. The copy is NOT read-only: it is the copier's own content, makes no claim about anybody else's bytes, and freezing it too would mean the next person needs a copy of the copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_Land . Land the train at the tested SHA candidate, extracted R1: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land (open question for the owner in the requirements note §6). Clears each member's trainId; its preview is then taken down by feature-staging.bpmn. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Land . Languages: extracted, rendered, and RTL candidate, extracted Every user-facing string reaches the .pot; every declared locale renders without clipping or overflow; right-to-left is laid out rather than mirrored by accident. New UI is where untranslated strings enter, because nothing was stale — there was nothing there before. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Locales . Lay out the options, with what each costs candidate, extracted Every option the agent could narrow the question to, each with what it costs and what it makes hard to undo. Narrow from context first: an option the agent could have ruled out itself wastes the reader's attention. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_LayOutOptions . Leave a reachable way back candidate, extracted Leave the way back reachable: the collapsed window becomes a control in its own position and focus moves to it — left alone, focus lands on <body> and the keyboard position is lost. An action whose inverse is not reachable is not a toggle (bean l4zi). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_OfferWayBack . Leave it referenced, record why candidate, extracted A refusal is not a failure of the process — it is the process working. The node stays referenced, which means the graph still knows it exists and where, and the refusing gate's basis is recorded so the next caller does not re-litigate it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_StayRef . Leave it alone (coordinate instead) candidate, extracted Never resolve, scrap or delete a bean another session or a human owns. Claiming is how two sessions avoid picking the same item; closing someone else's is how one of them loses work it had not finished reporting. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_LeaveAlone . Leave the content exactly where it is candidate, extracted The reader said no: nothing moves, no position is dropped, and the board is left exactly as it was. Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_Cancel . Link L1 nodes into the corpus graph candidate, extracted Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact -- paper, L2, L3 -- resolves to it through library/. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Link . Link the work to an issue candidate, extracted Feature work must be linked to a GitHub issue. Scan before creating, and never create one without the BA's permission — an issue is the stakeholder's record, not the agent's scratchpad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Issue . Link to existing issue candidate, extracted A match was found: ask the person whether the requirements go on #NNN, then link the work there. The issue is where stakeholders sign off, so no phase proceeds without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_LinkIssue . Link to the enterprise architecture candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 6. Assess the digital health enterprise architecture, identify the common and enabling components and shared services that make up the digital health platform, and link the investment to both. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_LinkEnterpriseArchitecture . List the harnesses this could be candidate, extracted Zero or more. The candidate everybody has is bootstrap itself. Context may name others: "please set up <owner>/<repo> here" names one, and so does any Harness built on bootstrap that the Requestor mentions. This step narrows; it does not decide. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListHarnesses . Both are Knowledge Graph Data Stores; the difference is only how they are reached. A location whose root already holds a declaration, <name>.json, is not a blank slate, and says so in the question. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListLocations . List the steps the declarations name candidate, extracted In the order of the table in initialization-steps: declaration, needs, each dependency's instructions, the documents at their IRIs (checked above, and listed first), directories, assets, README, README sections, site. Each step names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_ListSteps . List upstream releases and compare to the pin candidate, extracted git ls-remote --tags, filtered by the row's tagPattern and ordered by version. Nothing is cloned and no API token is needed, so the check runs the same way on a laptop and in CI. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_QueryUpstream . Load or reuse the warm context (fhir_context_load) candidate, extracted The validator's server mode holds the loaded dependency packages, snapshots and expansions in its session cache. Cold start loads the restored derived FHIR rather than regenerating it. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_ContextLoad . An id naming no shipped voice is an error rather than a skip — a folio that believes it is applying a voice and is applying nothing has the cleanest-looking output of the three. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_LoadActive . A command run goes in execution (command, exit code, where output went) — never the output itself, and never a secret, token or credential: capture on puts entries in git. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogMessage . Log findings on the bean [todo-manager] candidate, extracted Validation failed: record the findings on the change's bean, so the work plan says what blocks it. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_LogFindings . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_LogFindings . Log task-end candidate, extracted Write a task-end entry, with the outcome in the detail. The step is the unit: an entry per step, not one when the whole process finishes, or every intermediate entry is lost. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogEnd . Log task-start candidate, extracted Write a task-start entry before touching anything: summary, actor, and the process/task/bean/branch/session it belongs to where they exist. role, process and task are optional on purpose — do not invent a lane for work done outside a process. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogStart . Log the environment error on the bean [todo-manager] candidate, extracted Exit 2 from restore: the cache store or the toolchain could not be reached. Record that on the change's bean, with the restore output, so the work plan says the build did not run and why. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. 12370.title: M
12370.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. An agent may be dispatched to run it on its own: it needs nothing but that diagram and the declarations. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_CompleteInitialization . Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this Tool's subprocess rather than by the general step (owner, 2026-10-01: "need to create gh-pages branch before can turn on"). In order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). Each half is done, not done, or could not be determined; never assumed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Provision . Make the change candidate, extracted The loop's only open-ended step. Everything around it is procedure; this is the work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Implement . Make the value proposition and set next steps candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 9. The case made to whoever pays, and what follows. Scaling up is a different method and a different publication — 9789241509510-eng, The MAPS Toolkit — which begins where this implementation ends. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_ValueProposition . Map L2 → L3 [l3-fhir-authoring] candidate, extracted Each data element becomes a profile, each value set a ValueSet, each decision a PlanDefinition / Library. The DAK's L2 content is l3-fhir-authoring's sourceModel; this step binds l2-dak-authoring beside it, which is where the WHO L2 → L3 ordering lives now that the generic skill names no DAK (smart-* separation stage D, #1767). BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_MapL2 . Map the current state and confirm bottlenecks candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 3.1. Determine the health programme processes to target, map their workflows, identify and confirm bottlenecks. Then 3.2, a root cause analysis. This is where DIIG builds on CRDM, and it says so: "This process builds on the Public Health Informatics Institute's Collaborative Requirements Development Methodology (CRDM)". Its three areas of concentration are business process analysis, business process redesign and requirements definition — two of which name diagrams this platform already executes. They are parallel tracks, not a composite: pick one per decision and name it. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_MapCurrentState . Map values onto the shared palette ROLES candidate, extracted surface / ink / edge / accent, shared across every kind. A palette per kind would be three spellings of "accent colour", free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/ingest-theme.bpmn#Task_MapRoles . Materialise the part [materialize-remote] candidate, extracted The ONLY way bytes arrive. Purpose first, then the five gates — size, restrictions, copyright, retention, source loss — then fetch with fixity, or stay referenced with the refusing gate's basis recorded. Both ends of that subprocess return here and the walk continues: one part refused is not the subscription refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Materialize remote content (the five gates) candidate, extracted The shared subprocess. It resolves the request against the source descriptor, then asks size, restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, and either fetches with fixity or leaves the content referenced. This process does not restate any of that; it waits for the outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Measure the signals candidate, extracted Files and bytes per instance, clone cost (bun run health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate's cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package's import cone. Recorded in the bean; none alone is a trigger. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Measure . Mechanical checks, both viewports candidate, extracted Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Check . Merge each member onto the base [merge-base] candidate, extracted merge-base.bpmn once per member, in order, --no-regen; then ONE bun run regen over the result. Tool: merge:train. Always onto the current base, never a cached one (R5). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Call_MergeMembers . Merge main in, regenerate, fix mechanical gates candidate, extracted Merge commits only; never a force-push. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_AgentFix . Merge restored and rebuilt records candidate, extracted Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone's freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact's record and never re-derives one. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the base in, without committing candidate, extracted git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main on a clean tree (untracked files refuse too, so the final stage cannot sweep in a scratch file). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge, on explicit confirmation candidate, extracted The owner says "merge it", and only then is the branch merged. Merge to main triggers: 1. the main site rebuilds with the changes; 2. the staging preview's cleanup runs; 3. the review comments committed on the feature branch land on main, as the review record. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_Merge . Monitor, and use data effectively candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 8. Establish a logic model, plan the monitoring and evaluation, establish a culture of data use, and manage adaptively — using the data to optimize the interventions rather than only to report on them. The full treatment of this chapter is a separate publication in this library, 9789241511766-eng, Monitoring and Evaluating Digital Health Interventions. It is a parallel track, not a sub-step: do not blend the two. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_MonitorAndUseData . Mount the branch tip at the declared path candidate, extracted A branch source keyed by tip: branch-store mount --id <dir-id> writes the tip's files at the declared path, so every reader finds the directory where it always was; push splices edits back onto the tip, never forcing, and a same-file race is a conflict. The branch's NAME is the special-branches row the resolver attached — a branch no row declares is refused rather than guessed. A commit-keyed branch is read per commit through its own store (qa-store), not mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountBranchTip . Move into library/<bib-slug>/ candidate, extracted The folder name IS the bibliography citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Promote . Move the entry's ref and re-cache the declaration candidate, extracted Only after every held part has been through the refresh. Moving the ref first would make the records of parts not yet refreshed describe a commit the entry no longer names. The cached declaration is replaced so the review that follows shows what the NEW pin offers, including subgraphs that did not exist at the old one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_RePin . Move the pin and open the PR candidate, extracted The pin literal moves in the one file upstream-pins.json declares, and the PR body says what the version range changed in RENDERED output — the evidence, not just the verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_ApplyPin . MVP: build the candidate on a staging branch candidate, extracted An MVP is a DEPLOYED BUILD, not a description of one. The pin is moved on a branch and feature-staging.yml publishes it under STAGING/<branch-slug>/, so the reviewer looks at the artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Task_Mvp .

12371.title: N
12371.content: Name the subject and the level candidate, extracted One sentence naming WHAT is being analysed and at WHICH level — individual, organisational, national, international. The source requires this before anything is listed: "the classification of a variable also depends on the purpose of the practice", and the criteria for assigning a variable to a quadrant "may be more difficult to clarify if the methodology is not used for a company but for a country". It also bounds the known limitation that SWOT "is rarely deployed at lower than the organization level", where one scan drives strategy for units its factors do not hold equally for. Naming the level does not remove that risk; it makes it visible in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_FrameSubject . Name the substrate, pin a full commit SHA candidate, extracted owner/repo and a 40-character commit SHA — never a branch, never an abbreviated SHA. The schema refuses anything else (SubscriptionSchema.ref), and this step exists so the refusal is met while choosing rather than at commit time. A tag replaces the SHA only once the substrate publishes releases. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Pin . Name what will move, and where it lands candidate, extracted Before anything moves, name the content that would move — what it is, with its size and age — and where it lands. The confirmation sits in front of the move: an agent never relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_AskConfirm . Narrative description per image, localized candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED. Tracked as a bean; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF, not only to an uploaded one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Image . Narrative review candidate, extracted Descend into Process_NarrativeReview. The actor takes on the narrative-reviewer lane for this call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_NarrativeReview . Note the main-branch watch [watch] candidate, extracted Second dispatch point: the change was approved and merged, and the root of the site has been rebuilt from main. This is the moment docs-site.yml failed all 30 times over two months (bean xom7) while looking exactly like a green run from inside the repo. note rather than claim, and the difference is not cosmetic. By here the branch-watch bean already exists, and whether the publish SUCCEEDED is a judgement this step cannot make -- the build reports its own exit code, and xom7 is the record of that being believed. AGENTS.md: a bean is not closed on someone else's say-so. So the step records what it observed and leaves the verdict to the watcher. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_WatchMainCI . Note the missed coupling on the bean [todo-manager] candidate, extracted Append to bean a9tx (W8): the resource key, the differential path, and why it is unexplained. Check before creating: beans create is not idempotent. A note, not a new bean, unless the owner asks for one. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn#Task_FileCoupling .

12372.title: O
12372.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn#Task_Ocr . Offer the knowledge-graph destinations for the agreed set candidate, extracted THE STEP THAT WAS MISSING. Requirements were elicited, agreed and signed off, and then existed as an issue and a conversation — so the output of the process that exists to produce durable requirements was the one thing the knowledge graph never learned. ONE question for the SET, not one per requirement: a six-phase run can agree many, and asking six times is the same failure as a form that re-asks what it was already told. The options are DERIVED from the graphs this instance declares in <name>.json, read at the time of asking, so an instance that adds a graph gets it in the offer without anybody editing a skill. Never a list typed from memory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_OfferKg . Open a bean for the unverified citation [todo-manager] candidate, extracted An unresolvable citation is not dropped and not silently kept. It becomes a tracked item, so the gap is visible in the work plan rather than surviving as a footnote nobody re-checks. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_RecordUnverified . Open beans for the change requests [todo-manager] candidate, extracted Each requested change becomes a bean, so the editors and agents picking the work up next see exactly what review asked for and what is still open. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_OpenChangeBeans . Open or claim the release bean [todo-manager] candidate, extracted The release itself is a bean: it carries what is in this draft, what is outstanding, and who is holding it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_OpenReleaseBean . Open or close a role to an actor candidate, extracted The join every other diagram depends on. An empty roles is a DETERMINED empty — it says the actor takes on none — and is not the same as an absent one, which asserts nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AssignRoles . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted Findings: EDIT the one open issue labelled ci-health if there is one, otherwise create it, with the report as the body. One issue edited in place, never a new issue or a comment per run, so the tracking issue never becomes a feed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/ci-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Track . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted Findings: EDIT the one open issue labelled pr-no-checks if there is one, otherwise create it, with the sweep's report as the body. One issue edited in place, never a new issue or a comment per run, so the tracking issue never becomes a feed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/pr-checks-present.bpmn#Task_Track . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted Findings: EDIT the one open issue labelled repo-health if there is one, otherwise create it, with the report as the body. One issue edited in place, never a new issue or a comment per run, so the tracking issue never becomes a feed. The body states that nothing in it has been acted on. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/repository-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Track . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted One issue, edited in place. GitHub's own failure mail is the channel that was already ignored thirty times, so this adds none: an edit does not notify, and a pin that stays behind for two months stays one unread item rather than nine. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_TrackIssue . Open the branch-watch bean [watch] candidate, extracted First dispatch point for a CI watcher: the feature branch has changed and a staging build now exists to watch. The watcher is DISPATCHED BY OPENING A BEAN, not by a workflow_dispatch -- per the owner on bean 29ij, this is a task/workflow initiation. That is the whole reason it is an activity rather than a line of prose. A bean makes the watch durable past the session that opened it: the container is reclaimed, and what survives is the claim. Starting the watcher and recording that it is running are ONE declared step, so the two cannot disagree about whether anything is watching. Claim rather than note: the watch is work in progress, and it is idempotent, so re-entering on a subsequent push does not duplicate it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_WatchBranchCI . Open the rule's citation candidate, extracted Every rule resolves to a real library/ section or a KG node, and carries the quote it was read from. Opening it is what lets a reviewer say WHY the rule applies — and it is the only way to catch a rule that misread its own source. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_OpenCitation . Open the session record candidate, extracted Writes id, actor and startedAt, with open and claimed empty. An empty open is the NORMAL state, not an unfinished one: an agent reading, answering or deciding is in no process at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_OpenSession . Open the tracking issue, naming the failed step candidate, extracted Open the issue with the step that failed, the run link and — for a verification failure — the verifier report. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/publish-alert.bpmn#A_Open . Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. NOT between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision, which is the pair the work-plan named — in this diagram those run the OTHER WAY ROUND. Flow_21b goes Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision that has already been recorded, and interposing there would analyse options after the choice was made. In the Agent lane, and this diagram makes the reason sharp. Task_RecordDecision is a userTask in Lane_Editor that already names decision-audit, and Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note. Those are two different acts — the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED, the editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN — and putting the analysis in the editor's lane would collapse them, making the same party both analyse and decide. The subprocess's own documentation refuses that: it produces options and a recommendation, and the authorisation belongs to the calling step. CallActivity_Evidence sits in Lane_Editor instead, and that is not an inconsistency: the author performs the evidence retrieval, whereas here the point is that the analyst is not the decider. On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis adopt · hold · decline candidate, extracted On the single edge into PM_Decide, and deliberately not earlier: the MVP build and its gates are HOW the options' costs are measured, so an analysis before Task_Mvp would weigh alternatives against no evidence. Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. NOT between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact, although that is the handoff the work-plan named. Those two tasks are in DIFFERENT LANES with no sequence flow between them — the agent's assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter, not directly — so there was no edge there to interpose on. The conceptual handoff is real; the edge was not. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the Review Committee lane is where a decision is taken. A subprocess in the reviewer's lane would read as the committee analysing its own options, which is a different process. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator does not, and this is the diagram where that distinction has teeth, since Task_EditLogic feeds straight into the assessment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. Note where this is NOT. The work-plan named crdm-requirements-workflow, and A_Implement is not in that diagram — crdm-requirements.bpmn is the orchestrator, seven call activities and a gateway, and Phase 6 lives here in crdm-deliver.bpmn. The call goes where the step is, not where the plan said to look. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries cat-harness.processes:bean op="claim"; this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis .

Per option: what it does, its pro, its con, what it changes DOWNSTREAM, and how reversible it is — laid out where the rows can be read against each other, then one recommendation and a stated default. A step of its own rather than a line inside A_DefineReqs, because it has a different output and a different reader: the impact analysis is for the record, the comparison is the thing the BA answers from. Folding it in is how it gets skipped — the analysis feels finished, so the options go over as a list of names. Skipped legitimately when the analysis yields ONE viable approach. If the session cannot write where it belongs, draft it where it can, say so in the file, and open a bean to move it. Place it by hand, with a reason candidate, extracted Recorded as a queue entry whose placement is override with a position and a reason; the schema refuses one without a reason. It enters the next placement as the table's ownerOverride input. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Override . Place it in uploads/ by a declared route [upload-routes] candidate, extracted THE FIRST LINK, and it did not exist until 2026-09-30. Everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue: document-intake triggers on "User drops a file into uploads/", and both ingest Tools type their first input as "The upload to ingest, under the declared uploads graph". So the act of PUTTING it there was performed by three different mechanisms and governed by none of them. WHAT THIS STEP IS. Choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the instance that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one 404'd. WHY A PLAIN bpmn:task AND NOT A userTask. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is named "Contributor (human or agent)" precisely because both do — measured over this repository's own history, files have reached uploads/ in commits authored by Carl Leitner and in commits authored by Claude. Asserting human-only here would be the activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction written deliberately: the diagram saying one thing and the lane's role graph another. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer, which is the truth. WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility — three batches of PDFs arrived through the forge's web UI (c8349950fa5, f4ddfc65c8d, b8549160bb1) with no bean, no PR and no note, and the first sibling to notice was a generator going stale. A note against the ingestion bean is what makes the queue's growth something another session can see. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Place . Infrastructure; legislation, policy and compliance, including data management, privacy and security, and the regulation of new technologies; leadership and governance, including external partnerships; workforce and training; services and applications. The queue is declared with INSTANCE scope, so its declared path is missing the segment a repository-relative forge URL needs: /upload/main/uploads is a 404 and /upload/main/cat-harness/uploads is not, verified against GitHub 2026-09-20. Every failure is named — no origin remote, a non-GitHub forge, a declared-but-absent queue — because a URL is believed, and somebody sent to a wrong one cannot tell it from an empty directory. Folio-assistant dependency translations (depth-first walk) 3. WHO standard terminology (from smart-base) 4. Previous translations of related content . Prioritize the bottlenecks, then map the programme-specific ones onto the generic health system challenges. THE ARITHMETIC IS REFUSED HERE. DIIG Table 3.3.1 asks three questions, each scored 1-3 — how much impact does this bottleneck have on the process, what is the likelihood of overcoming it, is it important to a wide range of stakeholders — and sums them into a Score and a Prioritized Ranking. The three criteria are adopted whole; the total is not. Record each criterion's answer AND its reason, and order by argument. A ranked list reads as evidence in a way three stated judgements do not, and the weights were invented. Prose blocks enter the summary queue [library-ingestion] candidate, extracted Owner, 2026-09-24: "Make as QA sidecar as part of general doc ingestion to slowly drain." Nothing is written to ENQUEUE a block: the queue is derived (every prose block in every declared library, minus those whose summaries.json record is a current draft or confirmation), so a promoted entry is in it the moment its blocks are. A re-ingested document whose text changed re-enters it on its own, because the record's source_hash no longer matches. What an agent doing ingestion work does here is DRAIN a few: bun run summaries:next -- --n K hands it the next K blocks with their text, it writes a short summary of each in its own words, and bun run summaries:record writes them into library/<bib-slug>/summaries.json as drafts naming the agent and its model. The block itself stays verbatim and ingested. ADVISORY, never a gate: this step does not hold up Task_Citeable, and check:l1-complete reports the backlog (block-summaries) without failing on it. After Task_RepositoryGates, WHATEVER it concluded (needs: gates with always()), qa:publish --github writes this run's test/results trees to the orphan qa-reports branch: main/<sha>/ on a push to main, pr/<n>/<head-sha>/ on a same-repository PR (owner rulings D1, D3). A fork PR's token is read-only, so it is skipped with a ::notice naming why. It does NOT reach GW_Join: a red publish is its own red and never decides mergeability, and the hard gates never wait on it. The only job here holding contents: write, which is also how bun run gates knows not to run it locally. A CALL ACTIVITY: the key derivation, the fork skip and the never--f retry loop are qa-publish.bpmn, which also draws the retention run that takes entries off the branch again.
